issues.failure_explanation: The displayed reduction equates |I(h)-S(h)|/||h||_{H^alpha} with (int p_n rho)/(sum_{r=0}^alpha ||D^r p_n||^2). But the proof itself computes ||h_Lambda||_{H^alpha} = (sum_{r=0}^alpha ||D^r p_n||^2_{L^2_rho})^{1/2} and |I(h)-S(h)| = int p_n rho, so the right-hand side is missing a square root: as displayed the equation is false by a factor (sum_r ||D^r p_n||^2)^{1/2}. The transcribed univariate lower bound from the cited Theorem 3.2 drops the same square root; only with the root restored in both displays does the conclusion (>= c_alpha n^{-alpha/2}) follow.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the square root on the right-hand side of (eq:1d-RHS) and in the transcribed univariate bound, i.e. the denominator should be (sum_{r=0}^alpha ||D^r p_n||^2_{L^2_rho})^{1/2}, exactly as the proof's own norm computation gives; the cited lower bound then applies directly.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of thm:GH-lower-bound-general rests on a false displayed equation, and thm:lower-isotropic-Smolyak imports the same one-dimensional ratio (its proof states 'From the proof of Theorem thm:GH-lower-bound-general we know ... >= c_alpha n_{L-d+1}^{-alpha/2}'). No substantive claim, rate, or scope is lost once the forced correction is made.
issues.title: False reduction identity in the fooling-function argument: missing square root on the right-hand side of (eq:1d-RHS)
issues.why_classification: A single forced correction, visible directly from the norm computation in the same proof, restores the reduction and both dependent lower bounds with no change to any rate, constant dependence, or advertised scope.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated lower bound contains the parameter a, which is defined nowhere in the paper. The proof's first asymptotic, n_{L-d+1}^{-alpha/2} \asymp_d N^{-alpha/2} (ln n_{L-d+1})^{a(d-1)/2}, is valid only when a = alpha, since N \asymp_d n_{L-d+1} (ln n_{L-d+1})^{d-1}; for any other value of a the chain is false. Hence the statement is ill-defined as written, and the forced reading is a = alpha.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace a by alpha in the theorem statement and in the displayed chain in the proof; the proof then verifies the statement verbatim, with no change to any rate, hypothesis, or scope.
issues.overall_effect: The isotropic Smolyak lower bound is not a well-defined statement as printed; its intended content (logarithmic exponent alpha(d-1)/2) is recoverable only from the proof. No other labelled result uses the symbol a, and the abstract's description of the logarithmic factor is consistent with a = alpha.
issues.title: Undefined symbol a in the logarithmic exponent of the isotropic Smolyak lower bound
issues.why_classification: One forced substitution (a = alpha), dictated by the proof's own computation, repairs the statement completely; the conclusion and rate survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Counterexample: for d = 4 and n_{L-d+1} = e^3 (which satisfies the hypothesis n_{L-d+1} >= e^{d-1}), (ln n_{L-d+1})^{d-1} = 3^3 = 27 > e^3 = 20.09... = n_{L-d+1}.

issues.failure_explanation: The implication n >= e^{d-1} => (ln n)^{d-1} <= n is false for d >= 4 near the boundary: at d = 4, n = e^3 one has (ln n)^3 = 27 > e^3 ≈ 20.09. The needed conclusion ln N \lesssim_d ln n_{L-d+1} does not depend on this false step: from N \asymp_d n (ln n)^{d-1} one obtains ln N <= ln n + (d-1) ln ln n + O_d(1) <= d ln n + O_d(1), using only ln ln n <= ln n (valid since n >= e^{d-1} >= e), and the bounded range of n is absorbed into the constant c_{alpha,d}.

issues.title: False inequality '(ln n)^{d-1} <= n' claimed from n >= e^{d-1} (fails for d >= 4 near the boundary)
issues.why_classification: The false step is immaterial: the intended bound follows from a routine valid estimate with the same form of conclusion, so a short local repair preserves the theorem entirely.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
where $\mathscr{I}_{\ell}^{\mathrm{uni}}$ is the polynomial interpolation
operator using the zeros of $H_{n_{\ell}+1}$.

Counterexample: take n = 2 and alpha = 1, so p_2(t) = (1-t^2)/4 on [-1,1] (the zeros of H_2 are ±1). Then Q_2^{uni}(p_2) = 0 since p_2 vanishes at the nodes ±1, but the interpolant of p_2 at the zeros 0, ±sqrt(3) of H_3 is q(x) = (3-x^2)/12, and int q rho = (3-1)/12 = 1/6 != 0. Hence |int p_2 rho - Q_2^{uni}(p_2)| = int p_2 rho ≠ |int (p_2 - q) rho|.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof reduces the sparse-grid interpolation error to the univariate quadrature error via the identity |int p_n rho - Q p_n| = |int (p_n - I p_n) rho|, i.e. it uses int I p_n rho = Q p_n. But I^{uni} interpolates at the zeros of H_{n_l+1} while Q^{uni} is the Gauss-Hermite rule with nodes at the zeros of H_{n_l}; since the node sets differ, int I p_n rho = Q_{n+1}^{uni}(p_n) (exactness of the (n+1)-point rule on the degree-n interpolant), which is not equal to Q_n^{uni}(p_n) in general — in the displayed counterexample int I p_2 rho = 1/6 while Q_2^{uni}(p_2) = 0. Consequently the key comparison |int p_n rho - Q p_n|/||h|| <= ||h - I h||_{L^1}/||h|| is not justified, and both lower bounds of thm:added-1 (general and isotropic index sets) are unproven for the interpolation scheme as defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair for the interpolation scheme as defined; at minimum a repair must establish ||p_n - I^{uni} p_n||_{L^1_rho} >= c_alpha int p_n rho through a new one-dimensional argument (or a different fooling function). A bounded alternative is to redefine I^{uni} to interpolate at the zeros of H_{n_l} instead of H_{n_l+1}; then I^{uni}(p_n) = 0 and the existing argument closes, but the construction in the theorem statement changes.
issues.overall_effect: thm:added-1, the lower bounds for sparse-grid Gauss-Hermite interpolation in L^1_rho, is unsupported as written; no other result in the paper depends on it.
issues.title: Interpolation lower bound: false identity |int p rho - Q p| = |int (p - I p) rho| because the interpolation nodes (zeros of H_{n+1}) differ from the quadrature nodes (zeros of H_n)
issues.why_classification: The defective result is an auxiliary application and the paper's main theorems are unaffected, but for the interpolation scheme actually defined a genuinely new 1D lower-bound argument is required (not present in the source), while the only in-source fix modifies the definition of the interpolant; this is more than a typo yet causes no loss to the central claims.
